LanguageData.TF_UnknownTraitDesc: An unknown trait. It will reveal itself in time.
LanguageData.TF_MaterialTipDesc: Feels no pain, doesn't bleed or rot, and is immune to toxins. Butchering yields its material.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_LightsHint: Off: glowing creatures keep their look but light nothing up.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_LightFollowHint: How far a walking creature gets ahead of its light. Higher is cheaper with many glowing creatures; the light still recentres when it stops.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_EffectsHint: Embers, smoke and other effecters. Tints and glows always show.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_InheritHint: Multiplies each trait's own chance to pass to offspring.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_DiscoveryMessages: Message when a trait is discovered
LanguageData.TF_Settings_AbilityAI: Titans use trait abilities on their own
LanguageData.TF_Settings_AbilityAIHint: Hostile, manhunting and tamed titans cast their trait abilities in a fight, and wild ones when fighting back. Player colonists only cast when you order them to.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_ArmorHint: Share of the stuff's armor value. Steel at this setting: +{0} sharp armor.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_DamageHint: How strongly the stuff's damage multipliers apply. 0%: every material hits like flesh.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_FireHint: How much flammability changes fire damage and ignition. At this setting: wood takes x{0} fire damage, stone x{1}.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_ButcherHint: A steel bear (body size 2.15) gives about {0} steel.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_PreciousHint: Extra units for small-volume stuffs like gold and silver, as vanilla does.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_MarketValueHint: A tamed jade bear counts its jade toward colony wealth (and raid size).
LanguageData.TF_Settings_ValuePercent: Market value per trait point (% of creature's value)
LanguageData.TF_Settings_ValuePercentHint: Scales with the species: the same trait is worth far more on a thrumbo than on a rat. Drawbacks with negative points lower the value.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_ValueFlatHint: Added on top of the percentage, so small titans still count. Colony wealth, and so raid points, include every trait, known or not. Trade prices and the info card include only discovered traits.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_MysteryHint: Traders pay this much more (of the creature's normal value) for a creature with any undiscovered trait.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_PointTargetHint: Used when a mod rolls traits without its own target. Traits are rolled until their points reach the target; the last one may go over.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_StrictnessHint: How rarely a trait worth more than the points left still rolls. 0: the target is only a minimum. Higher keeps titans close to their target.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_DrawbackHint: A titan that rolls the chance can take drawbacks. Their negative points are paid back with more or better traits.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_UtilityHint: Utility traits (meaty, pack beast and the like) get their own roll after the others, in any trait slots left. Their points are this share of the titan's target, at least one common trait's worth, and add no health.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_RarityShiftHint: Chance an inherited scaling trait is born one rarity higher or lower than its parent's (even odds either way).
LanguageData.TF_Settings_RarityWeightsHint: Relative weight of each rarity when a trait is rolled.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_RarityStrengthHint: How much stronger a scaling trait's effects are at each rarity.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_RarityPointsHint: What a trait is worth at each rarity: its cost when rolling, and its health and market value.
LanguageData.TF_DietCardNote: Changed by this creature's material and known titan traits.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_HealthPerPointHint: Each trait point makes every body part this much tougher. Utility trait points don't count. Traits can add more of their own.
LanguageData.TF_Card_TraitsIntro: Rare traits this creature was born with. Unknown traits reveal themselves in time, and offspring can inherit any of them.
LanguageData.TF_Card_Mystery: Traders pay {0} more for a creature with unknown traits.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_EatMaterial: Nutrition from eating own material (per unit)
LanguageData.TF_Settings_EatMaterialHint: A hungry material creature with no other food eats its own material: {0} units fill 1 nutrition. Tamed ones eat from your stockpiles unless the stack is forbidden; wild ones eat any they find.
LanguageData.TF_Settings_EatMaterialOffHint: Material creatures don't eat their material.
LanguageData.TF_PackCalled: {PAWN_labelShort} called its pack. {1} came to fight.
LanguageData.TF_HydraSplit: {PAWN_labelShort} split as it died. {1} young ones sprang from its body.
